title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section 5, from the previous page): M is a free Z/4-module of rank 2. M_0 = M/2M is an F_2-plane. J = M_0^* is the set of the three NONZERO vectors x_i of M_0; the * means 'minus zero', not the dual. The sequence 0 -> M_0 --2--> M -> M_0 -> 0 makes each fibre M_i (the preimage of x_i) an M_0-torsor. The relation sum x_i = 0 trivializes the contracted product of the M_i. So the product torsor M_J (under M_0^J) descends to a torsor P_M under V_J(M_0) = ker(sum: M_0^J -> M_0).

This page:
(9) Giving the M_i together with that trivialization is the same as giving P_M, with M_i = P_M pushed out along pr_i.

Margin (11): M_0 = F_2^J/diag, via (a_i) -> sum a_i x_i, whose kernel is the diagonal. Hence Hom(M_0, W) = V_J(W) for any W.

(12) With W = M_0 this gives the canonical isomorphism End(M_0) -> V_J(M_0), u -> (u(x_i))_i. Both sides have dimension 4. The note End = M_0^v (x) M_0 = M_0 (x) M_0 uses the canonical self-duality coming from Lambda^2 M_0 = F_2.

(13) An S_3-equivariant embedding M_0 -> End(M_0). It sends 0 -> 0 and x_i -> sigma_i, the unique involution (transvection) fixing x_i and swapping x_j, x_k. Additivity holds because sigma_1 + sigma_2 + sigma_3 = 0 (evaluate on each x_i).

(14) An embedding F_2^omega -> End(M_0). Here omega is the 2-element set of cyclic orientations of J, identified with the two 3-cycles rho, rho' = rho^{-1} in S_J = GL(M_0). Since rho^2 + rho + 1 = 0, we get rho + rho' = id. So the constant function 1 goes to id, and the image is the field F_4 = F_2[rho] inside End(M_0).

Finally sigma_i, sigma_j, rho, rho' form a basis. Hence End(M_0) = M_0 (+) F_2^omega, a canonical S_3-module decomposition of M_2(F_2): the projective simple 2-dimensional module plus the permutation module on S_3/A_3. The decomposition is canonical because each summand has no nonzero equivariant maps to the other.

Purpose (next page): split the torsor P_M into a pair (I_M, S_M) of torsors under M_0 and under F_2^omega. This yields:
- an equivalence of groupoids {free rank-2 Z/4-modules} = {triples (M_0, I, S)};
- the split extension GL_2(Z/4) = M_2(F_2) x| GL_2(F_2), with M_2(F_2) = F_2^2 (+) F_2^omega as S_3-modules;
- SL_2(Z/4) characterized through sign(g) * e(Tr u).

This is preparation for describing level-4 structures on elliptic curves away from characteristic 2, i.e. torsors under the 2-torsion plus orientation data related to the Weil pairing mod 4.
errors: No mathematical errors. The relation is written 'rho + rho' + 1 id = 0' and then 'rho + rho' = id'; these agree over F_2.

Minor gap: before concluding that the P_M torsor splits canonically, one should note that the decomposition End(M_0) = M_0 (+) F_2^omega is S_3-equivariant and canonical. This holds since M_0 is projective-simple and there are no nonzero equivariant maps between the two summands; it is not stated explicitly here.

ideas.what: Descending the product of the fibre torsors M_i (over the three nonzero vectors of M/2M) to a torsor under V_J(M_0) = ker(sum), using sum x_i = 0
ideas.modern_name: torsor description of an extension class / pushout and contracted product of torsors
ideas.where_published: general formalism in SGA 4 / SGA 7 (Exp. VII); not this specific application

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism End(M_0) = V_J(M_0) = Hom(F_2^J/diag, M_0) for an F_2-plane
ideas.modern_name: linear algebra of the F_2-plane; S_3 = GL_2(F_2) as permutations of the 3 nonzero vectors

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant decomposition M_2(F_2) = M_0 (+) F_2^omega, with M_0 spanned by the transvections and F_2^omega = F_4 = F_2[3-cycle] indexed by the cyclic orientations of J
ideas.modern_name: decomposition of the adjoint module of GL_2(F_2); F_4 as the centralizer of a Singer cycle

ideas.what: Use toward GL_2(Z/4) = M_2(F_2) x| GL_2(F_2) and a groupoid classification of rank-2 Z/4-modules by (M_0, M_0-torsor, F_2^omega-torsor)
ideas.modern_name: structure of GL_2(Z/4Z) and level-4 structures on elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (structure of congruence quotients; Klein/Fricke era for level 4)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary linear algebra over F_2 and torsor bookkeeping toward the known split structure of GL_2(Z/4Z). The canonical, choice-free formulation via orientations of J is stylistically Grothendieckian, but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Marginal NB (11): read roughly as 'pour [un] vectoriel W, V_J(W) = Hom_{F_2}(M_0, W) car M_0 = F_2^J/diag'. It is not 'Hom(M_0, omega)'.
The '(13)' at the top is the page/section number of the notes; the equation labelled (13) is the separate one lower down.
J = M_0^* denotes the set of nonzero elements of M_0, not the dual space.
Last lines: likely 'donc que sigma_i, sigma_j forment une base de M_0, et rho, rho' de F_2^omega ...'.
